title: Is the four-day week the future?
title_es: ¿Es la semana de cuatro días el futuro?

questions.q: According to the text, why did some industrialists support a five-day week?
options: Workers with free time would also become consumers
Workers with more free time would produce more goods
The law forced them to give two days off
Workers refused to come in on Saturdays
questions.answer: Workers with free time would also become consumers
questions.why: Dice: workers with more free time would also become consumers.

questions.q: What was the main condition of the 2022 UK trial?
options: Productivity had to stay the same
Workers had to accept a fifth less pay
Companies had to hire more staff
Only managers could take part
questions.answer: Productivity had to stay the same
questions.why: Dice: productivity had to stay the same.

questions.q: Most companies decided to return to the five-day week after the trial.
Which benefit for companies is mentioned?
options: Staff took fewer sick days
Profits doubled in six months
Offices became cheaper to run
Meetings became longer and better
questions.why: Dice: staff took fewer sick days.

questions.q: Why do critics doubt the results can be applied everywhere?
options: Most participants were small office-based firms
Most participants were hospitals and schools
The trial lasted only six weeks
Workers lied in the surveys
questions.answer: Most participants were small office-based firms
questions.why: Dice: Most of the participating firms were small and worked in offices.

questions.q: What risk does 'cramming five days into four' involve?
options: Longer, more intense days that move the stress elsewhere
Lower salaries for exactly the same amount of work as before
More unnecessary meetings each week
Fewer holidays during the year
questions.answer: Longer, more intense days that move the stress elsewhere

options: Results may matter more than hours spent working
The four-day week should be compulsory for every company
The experiment was a costly failure
Hospitals should be the first to try it
questions.answer: Results may matter more than hours spent working
questions.why: Último párrafo: medir resultados y no horas.

questions.q: The tone of the article is best described as…
options: balanced and analytical
angry and critical
humorous and lighthearted
purely promotional
questions.why: Presenta argumentos a favor y en contra antes de concluir.

questions.q: Find an expression in paragraph 1 meaning 'accepted without question': the five-day week was taken for ___.
questions.why: Take for granted = dar por sentado.

task: ¿Apoyarías una semana laboral de cuatro días en tu país? Escribe 120–150 palabras con argumentos a favor y en contra y tu conclusión.
paragraphs: For most of the twentieth century, the five-day working week was taken for granted. It had been introduced, in part, by industrialists such as Henry Ford, who realised that workers with more free time would also become consumers. A century later, a growing number of companies are asking whether it is time for another change.

In 2022, one of the largest trials of a four-day week took place in the United Kingdom. Around sixty companies, employing nearly three thousand people, reduced working hours by roughly a fifth without cutting pay. The condition was simple: productivity had to stay the same. At the end of the six-month trial, the vast majority of the companies chose to continue with the new schedule, and several made it permanent.

Supporters argue that the results speak for themselves. Employees reported lower levels of stress and burnout, slept better and found it easier to balance work with family responsibilities. Companies, for their part, noted that staff took fewer sick days and that it became easier to attract and keep talented workers. Some managers also discovered that many meetings were simply unnecessary.

Critics, however, warn against drawing conclusions too quickly. Most of the participating firms were small and worked in offices, where output is relatively easy to reorganise. It is far harder to imagine a hospital, a school or a factory operating at the same level with a fifth less time, unless more staff are hired, which increases costs. Others point out that cramming five days of work into four can make each day longer and more intense, simply moving the stress elsewhere.

Perhaps the most interesting effect of the debate is that it has forced organisations to question how they measure work. If what matters is results rather than hours spent at a desk, then the length of the week may become less important than how wisely those hours are used.
